mechanism_narrative: The current federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is inversely related to S&P 500 20-day forward returns; lower rates compress discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns in periods with FEDFUNDS < 1.0% are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6.0% with positive 3-month change signals labor market deterioration, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns in triggered instances (UNRATE > 6.0% and 3m change > 0) are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When both GDP (GDPC1) and industrial production (INDPRO) are below their 12-month moving averages, it signals economic weakening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns in triggered instances (both below 12m_MA) are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 2.0% and rising for 6 months), S&P 500 produces negative returns over the next 60 trading days as the economy slows and profit growth decelerates.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns in triggered instances (FEDFUNDS > 2.0% and 6m change > 0) are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The current level of housing starts (HOUST) is positively related to S&P 500 20-day forward returns; higher housing activity signals strong economy and robust consumer spending, leading to positive equity returns.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns in periods with HOUST > 950.0 are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 900.0, it signals a weakening housing market, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns in triggered instances (HOUST < 900.0) are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 900.0 and CPIAUCSL is below 238.0, it signals weak housing market and low inflation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the Fed maintains dovish stance.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns in triggered instances (HOUST < 900.0 and CPIAUCSL < 238.0) are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During labor market tightening cycles (PAYEMS growth rate < 0.5% for 3 months), S&P 500 produces negative returns over the next 60 trading days as the economy slows and corporate profits face headwinds.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns in triggered instances (PAYEMS 3m growth rate < 0.5%) are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.
